15# Kunlunxin (XPU) override of special_log_ndtr / special_log_ndtr_ 

16# (aten::special_log_ndtr), log Phi(x) for the standard normal CDF Phi. 

17# 

18# Why an override exists (two independent HEAD defects, both measured on XPU 4): 

19# 

20# 1. CORRECTNESS. The generic `flag_gems/ops/special_log_ndtr.py:41` forms Phi 

21# first and takes the log afterwards: `log(0.5 * tl_extra_shim.erfc(-x/sqrt2))`. 

22# The XPU libdevice `erfc` (`_ZN3xpu4erfcEf`) links fine, but it is evidently 

23# `1 - erf`, so its *absolute* resolution is one ulp of 1 and its relative 

24# error grows like 1.2e-7/erfc(a) -- measured against a CPU float64 oracle 

25# (harness/probe/special_log_ndtr_erfc_accuracy_probe.py): 

26# a=1.99 -> 3.0e-5 a=2.48 -> 2.6e-4 a=3.00 -> 1.8e-3 

27# a>=3.92 -> erfc returns *exactly 0.0*, so log gives -inf. 

28# Taking the log of that reproduces the HEAD accuracy failures exactly 

29# (4 of 6 cases, `Greatest absolute difference: 0.1029`, mismatch 0.1% of 

30# lanes, i.e. the |x| > ~3.1 tail of randn), and makes every x < -5.55 lane 

31# return -inf where torch returns a large finite value. 

32# 2. PERFORMANCE. There was no vendor file at all, so the generic module kept 

33# the *generic* `flag_gems.utils.pointwise_dynamic` codegen (verified: 

34# `flag_gems.special_log_ndtr.__globals__["pointwise_dynamic"].__module__` 

35# was `flag_gems.utils.pointwise_dynamic`). That path runs at ~2.3 GB/s 

36# here: 57.9 ms for [4096,4096] fp32. 

37# 

38# Scheme (never forms Phi on the left tail, so it cannot underflow to -inf): 

39# za = |x| / sqrt(2) 

40# tt = 1 / (1 + za/2) 

41# P = Numerical-Recipes `erfcc` Chebyshev polynomial in tt (10 coeffs), 

42# for which erfc(za) = tt * exp(P - za^2) with |frac err| < 1.2e-7 

43# e = P - za^2 ( = log(erfc(za)) - log(tt) ) 

44# x <= 0 : log Phi(x) = e + log(0.5*tt) -- pure log space, no exp 

45# x > 0 : log Phi(x) = log1p(q), q = -0.5*tt*exp(e) -- 1-Phi is the small 

46# quantity here 

47# Validated in float32 arithmetic against a CPU float64 oracle over 

48# x in [-40, 10] (harness/probe/special_log_ndtr_scheme_check.py): max relative 

49# error 5.7e-7 on x <= 1, and log Phi(-40) = -804.6084 instead of -inf. 

50# 

51# log1p is NOT taken from the platform, for a measured reason 

52# (harness/probe/special_log_ndtr_log1p_probe.py, buckets of |y|): 

53# tl_extra_shim.log1p links, but it behaves like plain log(1+y): relative 

54# error 2.9e-3 at |y|=1e-5, 2.0e-1 at 1.5e-7, and it returns *exactly 0* for 

55# |y| < ~3e-8. Root cause is one level down: tl.log(s) near s=1 carries an 

56# absolute error of ~3.5e-8 (half an ulp of 1), and below 1-s ~ 1e-4 it 

57# returns literally s-1 (measured error == d^2/2 exactly, d = 1-s). 

58# So log1p(q) is built here as tl.log(s) + (q - (s-1))/s with s = 1+q: 

59# s-1 is exact by Sterbenz, so (q - (s-1)) is precisely the bit that rounding 

60# dropped, and adding it back divided by s recovers what tl.log lost. Measured 

61# |y|=1e-9..1e-4: relative error falls to <= |y|/2 (i.e. absolute error 

62# <= y^2/2 <= 5e-9) versus 1e0..3e-4 for the shim, and it is never worse. 

63# Residual: for |y| >~ 1e-4 the answer inherits tl.log's own 3.5e-8 absolute 

64# floor, so relative accuracy peaks around 3.5e-4 near x ~ 3.7 where 

65# |log Phi| ~ 1e-4. Left as is on purpose: the absolute error there is 

66# 3.5e-8, one ulp of 1, which is the platform's log floor, and buying relative 

67# accuracy would cost a third branch (extra tl.where ~0.11 ms + 3 fma). 

68# 

69# Symbol availability was established by real *compile* probes, one process per 

70# case (harness/probe/special_log_ndtr_symbol_probe.py) -- `hasattr` proves 

71# nothing on this backend. On XPU `tl_extra_shim` is 

72# `triton.language.extra.xpu.libdevice` (no `__nv_*` anywhere in it); each entry 

73# maps a dtype to an external symbol and the unavailable ones are literally 

74# spelled "Unsupported", which is what the linker then reports: 

75# erfc fp32 -> _ZN3xpu4erfcEf OK log1p fp32 -> _ZN3xpu6log1pfEf OK 

76# erf fp32 -> _ZN3xpu3erfEf OK exp/log -> Unsupported FAIL 

77# y0/y1/j0/j1/lgamma FAIL (matches the sibling bessel overrides) 

78# Hence exp/log below are core `tl.*` (both measured accurate to ~1 ulp away 

79# from 1), and no libdevice symbol is referenced by this file at all. 

80# 

81# Cost model (increment form, [4096,4096] fp32): 9 fma (Horner) + 1 div + 1 tl.log 

82# + 1 tl.exp + 1 div + 1 tl.where + ~7 mul/add on top of the ~0.13 ms pointwise 

83# floor -> ~1.2-1.5 ms predicted. 

84# 

85# Numeric constants are inline literals on purpose: a Triton @jit body cannot 

86# read module-level python globals, and inlining also means SpecOpRegistrar has 

87# no gems-level function reference left to leave pointing at a stale object. 

88# 0.7071067811865476 = 1/sqrt(2) 

89# No CPU/ATen/native/composite fallback; the whole evaluation is in the kernel. 

90import logging 

91 

92import torch 

93import triton 

94import triton.language as tl 

95from _kunlunxin.utils.codegen_config_utils import CodeGenConfig 

96 

97from ..utils.pointwise_dynamic import pointwise_dynamic 

98 

99logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

100 

101config_ = CodeGenConfig( 

102 512, 

103 (65536, 65536, 65536), 

104 32, 

105 True, 

106 prefer_1d_tile=True, 

107 buffer_size_limit=2048, 

108 isCloseVectorization=True, 

109 kunlunAutoGrid=True, 

110 unroll_num=8, 

111) 

112 

113 

114@pointwise_dynamic(promotion_methods=[(0, "DEFAULT")], config=config_) 

115@triton.jit 

116def special_log_ndtr_func(x): 

117 xf = x.to(tl.float32) 

118 za = tl.abs(xf) * 0.7071067811865476 

119 tt = 1.0 / (1.0 + 0.5 * za) 

120 

121 # Numerical Recipes `erfcc` polynomial: erfc(za) = tt * exp(P - za*za) 

122 p = -1.26551223 + tt * ( 

123 1.00002368 

124 + tt 

125 * ( 

126 0.37409196 

127 + tt 

128 * ( 

129 0.09678418 

130 + tt 

131 * ( 

132 -0.18628806 

133 + tt 

134 * ( 

135 0.27886807 

136 + tt 

137 * ( 

138 -1.13520398 

139 + tt * (1.48851587 + tt * (-0.82215223 + tt * 0.17087277)) 

140 ) 

141 ) 

142 ) 

143 ) 

144 ) 

145 ) 

146 e = p - za * za 

147 

148 # x <= 0: log(0.5*erfc(|x|/sqrt2)) evaluated entirely in log space. 

149 # x == +-0.0 -> tt = 1, P(1) ~ 1e-9 -> log(0.5) = -0.6931472 (matches) 

150 # x == -inf -> e = -inf, log(0.5*0) = -inf -> -inf (matches) 

151 # x == NaN -> NaN > 0 is False, so this branch, NaN (matches) 

152 left = e + tl.log(0.5 * tt) 

153 

154 # x > 0: q = -(1 - Phi(x)) is the small quantity, so build it and take 

155 # log1p(q) with the rounding bit of (1+q) added back explicitly. 

156 # x == +inf -> tt = 0, e = -inf, exp(e) = 0, s = 1 -> 0.0 (matches) 

157 q = -0.5 * tt * tl.exp(e) 

158 s = 1.0 + q 

159 right = tl.log(s) + (q - (s - 1.0)) / s 

160 

161 return tl.where(xf > 0.0, right, left).to(x.dtype) 

162 

163 

164def special_log_ndtr(A): 

165 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN SPECIAL_LOG_NDTR") 

166 if A.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32): 

167 raise ValueError( 

168 f"special_log_ndtr: unsupported dtype {A.dtype}, " 

169 "only float16, bfloat16 and float32 are supported" 

170 ) 

171 return special_log_ndtr_func(A) 

172 

173 

174def special_log_ndtr_(A): 

175 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN SPECIAL_LOG_NDTR_") 

176 if A.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32): 

177 raise ValueError( 

178 f"special_log_ndtr_: unsupported dtype {A.dtype}, " 

179 "only float16, bfloat16 and float32 are supported" 

180 ) 

181 special_log_ndtr_func(A, out0=A) 

182 return A
